newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian navy moves to combat oil smuggling at sea.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian navy moves to combat oil smuggling at sea.

text.p: Nigeria's navy has set up a unit to combat what it called illegal sale of oil products along the nation's coastal waters, the chief of naval staff said.

Rear Admiral Mike Akhigbe said in the southeastern oil city of Port-Harcourt at the weekend that the Directorate of Oil Movement and Maritime Services was set up after military ruler General Sani Abacha ordered that "economic saboteurs be routed."
"There is an existence of a mafia involved in large scale economic sabotage through the illegal sale of oil products outside Nigeria," Akhigbe said.
Crude oil exports account for more than 90 percent of total foreign exchange income of Nigeria.
Akhigbe said "the government plans to give economic saboteurs a hard knock in a manner more decisive and effective than the current efforts at sanitising our financial system."
Many bankers and businessmen alleged to have contributed to bank failures have either been jailed or are awaiting trial by failed bank tribunals set up last year by Abacha's government.
"We seek the cooperation of all maritime operators so that we can create a conducive atmosphere for those who do legal business at sea," Akhigbe said.
